minimum_generation_binding_contract: Treat the idempotency identity as at least {logical_effect_key K, payload identity/digest P, generation G}; bind it under the authority/fence that accepted it.
A committed record for K is duplicate-success only when the incoming payload and generation match the bound committed identity.
Reuse of K with mismatched payload or generation is a conflict, not a duplicate and not an overwrite opportunity.
If a new generation is legitimately required, establish a separately authorized supersession/new logical identity before issuing the effect; never silently reinterpret the old K.
Attempt identifiers are audit/retry-attempt metadata and cannot replace the stable bound logical identity.

weak_retry_rule.rule: If logical key K already exists, treat any later request carrying K as the same duplicate effect, even when payload or generation differs.
falsification: R_exact and R_payload_drift share K but request different payload identities; collapsing both to duplicate success loses the fact that P2 was never the committed effect.
R_exact and R_generation_drift share K but represent different generations; collapsing them aliases distinct intended generations and can return R1 as if G2 had executed.
Allowing overwrite instead is also unsafe because it destroys the stable replay meaning of K and can turn a retry into a second or mutated logical effect.

Therefore K alone is insufficient: exact payload/generation binding must be checked before duplicate-success; mismatches are hard conflicts unless an explicit supersession/new-identity protocol authorizes new work.

observations: Within the exact abstract fixture, the same logical key K can denote safe duplicate-success only when payload and generation match the committed bound identity K/P1/G1.

A key-only dedupe rule cannot distinguish exact replay from payload drift or generation drift, so it either falsely reports unexecuted work as successful or permits mutation/duplication under a supposedly stable key.

The minimum replay-safe checkpoint must preserve K together with payload identity and generation; a later retry may change attempt metadata but not the bound logical identity unless a separately authorized supersession/new-identity protocol exists.
inference: For the exact abstract C5-C7 replay tested, idempotent claim/effect identity must bind logical key, payload identity and generation under the accepting authority. Exact K/P/G equality can be reconstructed as duplicate-success; any payload or generation mismatch under the same K is a hard conflict absent an explicit supersession/new-identity protocol. This does not establish that any concrete Chat-exposed provider implements the required contract.
